FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Jndian Standards on 24 October 1989, after the draft finalized by the Chemical Engineering Plants and Related Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. Bio-gas plants are gaining lot of importance due to scarcity of conventional form of energy. This standard lays down the essential requirements and gives guidance for the design and construction of bio-gas plant. Bio-gas plant consists of a digester, gas storage unit, inlet and outlet pipelines. assembly and gas distribution

This standard was first issued in 1980 with a view to help the purchaser to design the capacities for his requirements of bio-gas so as to keep the cost of the plant to minimum. The standard was subsequently revised in 1986 based on the prevailing practices in the trade. In the present revision latest models of bio-gas plants being used in the country have been inculuded.

A separate Indian Standard IS 12986 ( Part 1 ) : 1990 `Biogas Plants - Glass fibre reinforced polyester resin gas holders : Part 1 With steel frame' has been pubiished for gas holders made of glass fibre reinforced polyester resin, for floating drum type bio-gas plants.

4.2 In KVIC model, the digester is an underground tank constructed in brick masonry, in accordance with SP 7 : 1983. RCC may also be used for constructing the underground tank. It has an inverted metallic/FRP drum which acts as gas holder. The gas holder moves up and down in a guide pipe. The gas produced in digester is collected in gas holder at a constant pressure. 4.3 In the pre-fabricated ferro-cement digester model, the digester is made of ferro-cement and other parts are same as KVIC model. 4.4 The Pragati model of bio-gas plant combine5 the merits of both the floating gas holder type and fixed dome type bio-gas plants. The foundation of this type of bio-gas plant is conical and the digester is shell-shaped. The inlet and outlet assemblies are almost the same as in the case of the floating gas holder type plant. There is a slight modification in the central guideframe and steel gas holder, so that the least load falls on the shell of the digester. 4.5 The Janta model bio-gas plant is a dome shaped underground construction. The masonry gas holder is an integral part of the digester. The gas produced in digester is collected at variable pressure by displacement of slurry to inlet and outlet. 4.6 Thr Dzenbnndhu model of bio-gas plant ha\ been de\igncd on the basis of fixed-domcbio-gar plant\. The digester is connected with the inlet and the outlet tank. 5 CLASSIFICATION 5.1 Plants OF DIGESTERS Period 6.8 Gas Holder It is a storage tank for bio-gas. The gas outlet is at the top of gas holder. In floating drum designs, it is a separate component while in fixed dome designs it is an integral part of the digester. 6.9 Inlet It is for feeding the water to the digester. 6.10 Outlet It is for taking slurry. 6.11 Mixing out the digested portion c-f the mixture of bio-mass :lnd as a manure. It is also used for hastening the process of composting of other organic material. 6.7 Size/Rated Capacity of Bio-Gas Plant

The rated capacity of the plant is the approxlmate daily output of the gas in cubic metrc\ \vhich is produced by the plant when fed with prescribed quantity of bio-mass.

It is a gaseous mixture containing about 60 a high value fuel, about percent methane, 10 percent carbon-dioxide and traces of other gases, such as ammonia and hydrogen sulphide, obtained from anaerobic fermentation of biomass. 6.2 Bio-Mass This refers to bio-degradable material originating in land and aquatic environments. Cow dung is one of the most important and widely used bio-mass for the production of bio-gas. The Jung may be supplemented with other material like night soil, poultry droppings and excreta of other livestock. 6.3 Anaerobic Fermentation out by in the

9.1.4 Floating Gas Holder The gas holder consists of an inverted drum made of mild steel sheet or FRP. The mild steel gas holder shall be painted with one primer coat of red oxide as per IS 2074 : 1979 and two coats of black enamel paint as per IS 5661 : 1970. The gas holder floats up and down on a central guide pipe situated in the centre of the digester. The gas holder is rotated to break the scum-formed on the surface of the slurry in the digester. The gas holder helps in storing the gas and maintaining constant pressure. The details of the gas holder are shown in Table 1 read with Fig. 1.

pipes are connected to the digester near its bottom except for 1, 2 and 3 ms plants. The level of inlet shall be higher to that of outlet to ensure proper flow. The mixing tank may be made of brick masonry stone or other local material or RCC. The volume of the mixing tank shall be more than the daily input of the slurry. 9.1.6 Bio-Gas Outlet Pipe The gas outlet pipe is located in the top portion of the gas holder through which the gas flows out. 9.2 Fixed Dame Design The brief details of the different are indicated below. 9.2.1 Foundation The foundation is a compact base of the digester, constructed of stone chips/brick ballast and cement concrete. The upper portion of the foundation has a smooth plastered surface to prevent the seepage. 9.2.2 Digester The digester is a cylindrical tank resting on the foundation. The top surface of the foundation serves as bottom of the digester. The digester well is constructed of bricks and cement mortar. The digester has two small rectangular openings at the top situated diametrically opposite; one for the inflow of the feed and the other for the outflow of the digested slurry. 9.2.3 Gas Storage
It is constructed just above the openings in the digester for inflow and outflow of The height for gas storage is determined maximum volume of gas to be stored plant.

9 DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION

OF BIO-GAS PLANT 9.1 Floating Drum Design The brief details of the different are indicated below.
9.1.1 Foundation It is a compact base made of cement concrete and stone chips/brick ballast etc. The top surface of the foundation is smoothened by cement plaster to prevent any seepage.

components

components

9.1.2 Digester The digester is a cylindrical tank made of bricks and cement mortar or RCC. It is located on the top surface of foundation which also forms an integral part of the bottom of the digester. The inside of the digester is. smoothened by cement plaster. A ledge is built into the digester at a depth equal to that of gas holder's height. This arrests the gas holder from going down when no gas is,left in it and thus prevents the slurry from entering the gas pipe. Further, it guides all gas bubbles from the digester into the gas holder. A partition wall. separates this cylindrical digester pit into two halves except for 1, 2 and 3 ma sizes. 9.1.3 Guide Frame
It consists of central guide pipes fitted in a frame made of angle iron. It guides free up and <down movement of the gas holder.

Bureau of Indian

Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureazr oj'Z&an Standurds.4cl, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Dot : No. HMD 17 ( 5327 ).
